title: Lohagad Fort Murder: Accused Initially Planned to Injure Fiancé, Not Kill, Say Police
excerpt: Pune police reveal Siya Goyal and her boyfriend first researched ways to disable Ketan Agarwal before escalating their conspiracy to murder at the Maharashtra hill fort.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Siya Goyal and Chetan Chaudhary initially planned to injure Ketan Agarwal, not kill him.
  • The couple scouted multiple forts and watched suspense films before choosing Lohagad Fort for the murder.
  • Goyal attempted to push Agarwal off a cliff on June 14, claiming it was to save him from a snake.
  • Police are reconstructing events using eyewitness accounts, digital forensics, and CCTV footage after arrests on June 23.

Initial plan to injure, not kill

Pune Rural Police have disclosed that the two accused in the Lohagad Fort murder case originally conspired to injure, not kill, the victim — revealing a conspiracy that evolved over weeks from a plan to disable a man into a premeditated murder.

Siya Goyal, 20, and her boyfriend Chetan Chaudhary, 22, are in judicial custody for allegedly pushing her 26-year-old fiancé Ketan Agarwal into a 400-foot gorge at the historic Lohagad Fort near Pune on June 18. What was initially reported as an accidental fall during a trek has since been reclassified as a premeditated murder following a police investigation.

From Injury to Murder

According to police, Goyal and Chaudhary first discussed ways to injure Agarwal so severely that the wedding — scheduled for November in Jaipur — would be called off. “Their initial plan was only to injure him to make it appear like an accident,” a senior police officer told PTI on Tuesday.

The digital probe revealed that both accused had searched the internet for methods to make a person permanently disabled and how to slow-poison someone, according to the Pune Police. Goyal believed that by making Agarwal physically disabled, she could convince her family to cancel the marriage.

“She did not want to kill Ketan. She and her boyfriend tried different means to injure Ketan Agarwal but failed in their attempts. Finally, they conspired to push him into the 400-foot deep valley of Lohagad Fort.”

— Pune Police spokesperson

However, the pair grew anxious as Goyal and Agarwal’s pre-wedding trip to Bali approached in June. “When they realised that the idea to harm Agarwal was not feasible, they decided to execute the plan themselves,” the officer said. “They feared that if Agarwal survived and got wind of their conspiracy, he would expose them.”

Suspense Films and Scouting Missions

Police said the conspiracy evolved over several weeks, preceded by extensive online research and reconnaissance visits. The accused allegedly watched suspense films and browsed the internet before deciding that pushing Agarwal off a cliff would best resemble an accident.

The pair scouted multiple locations — Tiger Point in Lonavala, Visapur Fort, and several other forts in the region — before settling on Lohagad Fort. They exchanged photographs and assessed which location would leave behind the least evidence, according to investigators.

On May 31, Goyal visited Lohagad Fort with Agarwal in what police describe as a reconnaissance exercise. “The primary purpose was to identify a suitable spot from where the victim could be pushed,” the officer said, adding that Chaudhary deliberately stayed away to minimise risk.

Failed Attempts and Stolen Passport

The investigation has uncovered multiple prior attempts. Goyal allegedly stole Agarwal’s passport during a trip to Mumbai to derail their planned Bali vacation. On June 14, she reportedly made an unsuccessful attempt to push him off the cliff at Lohagad Fort, but Agarwal grabbed a bush and survived. Goyal told him she had pushed him to save him from a snake.

The fatal push came four days later, on June 18. Goyal and Agarwal — who had gotten engaged on February 19 and had been in a relationship that appeared normal to both families — returned to Lohagad Fort. This time, Agarwal did not survive the fall.

Investigation Deepens

Pune Rural Police said they have recorded statements from multiple eyewitnesses and are using them to reconstruct the sequence of events. Both accused reportedly deleted chats and communications after the incident, and police are investigating whether Goyal also wiped data from Agarwal’s phone.

The mobile phones of both accused have been sent for forensic examination. Investigators have also obtained records of their mobile and internet usage, and are working to corroborate physical evidence with CCTV footage, according to a senior officer.

Police further claim the two rehearsed the murder days earlier in an open area near a lounge in Pune’s Lulla Nagar. Both Goyal and Chaudhary remain in judicial custody.
